html:
The Kazakh Khanate was a nomad state on the steppes of what is now Kazakhstan, from the middle of the 1400s to the 1840s. The map spells it "Quazaq". It is the same state as the chart's Kazakh Khanate bar.

It began around 1465, when the princes Kerei and Janibek led their followers away from Abu'l-Khayr Khan, whose people became the Uzbeks. Both groups came out of the breakup of the Golden Horde. The name Kazakh is usually explained as "free wanderers".

The khanate was a loose union of herding clans grouped into three hordes, or jüz: the Senior, Middle and Junior. Khans held power through clan support, not a fixed bureaucracy. Raids by the Dzungars in the 1720s were so destructive that Kazakhs remember them as the Years of Great Disaster. Seeking help, the Junior jüz accepted Russian protection in 1731. Over the next century Russia abolished the khans' power horde by horde. The last great revolt, led by Kenesary Kasymov, ended in 1847.
